digest.component_or_area: code-review gate, per-pass model selection seam
propositions: The code-review gate's base, round_a, round_b, and coach steps inherit a single cfg.model implicitly instead of declaring per-pass model classes, preventing different models per LLM-calling step on non-default providers.

When a non-default provider (Bedrock) is configured, the single cfg.model knob forces all steps onto one model family, breaking the Pass-1/Pass-2/Pass-4 split (opus for Pass-1 finders, sonnet for Pass-2/Pass-4 verifiers) that the direct-Anthropic path achieves.

The verifier downgrade logic in verify.py:269 and completion.py:332 becomes unreachable or inverts on non-default providers because the equality test conflates an explicit operator override with a provider change, both arriving as cfg.model.

The batch steps (round_a, round_b) cannot declare their model at the step level because the batch runner ignores the step's model key and reads only the nested batch.model_ladder, creating a silent no-op trap for per-step declarations.

The code-review gate has no mechanism to express per-provider model mappings (e.g., Bedrock inference profile IDs), leaving the gate unrunnable on Bedrock with per-pass model control, blocking production cutover (eb6e) and parity comparison (0d76).
